summary: A Wikipedia-style overview of Houston, Texas, covering its rankings, geography, geology, demographics, government, economy, transportation, healthcare, arts, parks and disaster history. Houston is the most populous city in Texas and fourth most populous in the US, known for the Texas Medical Center, its energy-driven skyline, extensive freeway loops and a politically divided electorate.
one_line: Overview of Houston, Texas: its size, geography, demographics, government, economy, medical center, arts, transportation and hurricanes.
key_facts: Houston is the most populous city in Texas and fourth most populous in the US, with a census-estimated 2014 population of 2.239 million and a land area of 599.6 square miles.
Houston is the seat of Harris County and principal city of Houston–The Woodlands–Sugar Land, the fifth most populated US metropolitan area.
In 2008 Houston topped Kiplinger's Personal Finance Best Cities list and ranked second on the Fortune 500 list of company headquarters; in 2010 Forbes rated it the best city for shopping.

The Texas Medical Center has 49 non-profit member institutions, employs more than 73,600 people, and is where Life Flight was created; more heart surgeries are performed there than anywhere else in the world.
MD Anderson Cancer Center has ranked as one of the top two US cancer hospitals by U.S. News & World Report since 1990.
The JPMorgan Chase Tower, completed in 1982, is 75 floors and 1,002 feet tall, making it the tallest structure in Texas and 15th tallest building in the US.
Houston's freeway system uses loops: Interstate 610 (about 8-mile diameter), Beltway 8/Sam Houston Tollway (about 23 miles), and the proposed 180-mile State Highway 99 (Grand Parkway).
In 2009 Houston became the first US city with over 1 million people to elect a gay mayor, Annise Parker; the current mayor is Sylvester Turner, a Democrat.
Houston has a strong mayoral government with a mayor, city controller and 16 City Council members, and all Texas municipal elections are nonpartisan.
The Houston Theater District is the second-largest concentration of theater seats in a US downtown, with nine major performing arts organizations and six performance halls.

In the 2010 Census, whites were 51% of Houston's population (26% non-Hispanic whites), Blacks 25%, and Asians 6%; Hispanics were 37.4% in 2000 versus non-Hispanic whites 30.8%, down from 62.4% in 1970.
Houston sheltered more than 150,000 people from Hurricane Katrina in August 2005, and about 2.5 million residents evacuated for Hurricane Rita, the largest urban evacuation in US history.

Flat terrain and urban sprawl make flooding a recurring problem; downtown sits about 50 feet above sea level and the city turned from groundwater to Lake Houston, Lake Conroe and Lake Livingston because of subsidence.
Houston has the most total park and green space (56,405 acres) among the 10 most populous US cities.
In 2015 Southwest Airlines began international flights from Hobby Airport, the first since 1969.
